GP (short for Gear Points) is a Skell stat in Xenoblade Chronicles X that is analogous to . GP starts at 0, and increases through auto-attacks. Unlike TP, GP is only used to activate the Skell's Overdrive. In general, most Skells have a maximum GP of 3000. This can be increased by using the ground Augment Max GP Drive, or by using the Lailah or Skells which have a maximum GP of 6000. Unlike TP, which stays as long as the fighter does not get (or hit with attacks that drain TP), Skell GP slowly drains back to 0 (at a rate of 50 per second) if the pilot goes to the ground without the Skell. Gifting is a mechanic in Xenoblade Chronicles that allows the player to convert collectables into between party members. By selecting a collectable in the inventory (in the , this is done from the party instead), the player may use it as a "present" from one party member to another, which consumes the collectable and adds (or subtracts) a small amount of affinity between the two. Every party member has their own preference of collectables; the affinity gained (or lost) is based on the likes and dislikes of the receiver. HP (short for Health Points) is a Driver stat in Xenoblade Chronicles 2 and a Team stat in Torna ~ The Golden Country. It represents a combatant's health. A party member is incapacitated if their HP reaches zero. HP can be decreased by inflicting on an opponent, using certain moves that decrease a character's own HP, or falling from a significant height. It can also be healed through HP Potions, healing Driver Arts/Vanguard Arts/s, or effects from accessories or a character's . The HP of all party members is restored over several seconds when out of combat. Maximum HP can be increased by levelling up, equipping accessories that increase maximum HP, using s that passively increase maximum HP,
